messages:
Alex Chen: Heads up — Fiducia Bank POC kickoff next Tue. They require network design options for Private deployment (VPC) and want clear guardrails: no inbound internet, strict firewall allowlist, and static egress IPs for outbound to partner APIs. Asking for a short checklist + recommended approach by EOD today.

Priya Nair: Adding a short checklist here. TL;DR: PrivateLink + egress NAT/proxy gives best isolation without messing with customer routes. If customer mandates peering, we'll need non-overlapping CIDRs and route propagation rules.

Priya Nair: Checklist: 1) Customer VPC CIDR(s) 2) Can they accept AWS PrivateLink endpoints in their account? (yes/no) 3) Do they need static egress IP(s) for firewall allowlist? If yes, how many IPs? 4) Are TLS-inspection/proxy devices in-line that would break mTLS? 5) Which regions (us-west-2 / eu-west-1) for POC? 6) Any gov/regulatory HSM/KMS constraints?

Marco Ruiz: Quick network notes: - VPC peering = simple L3 routing but requires no CIDR overlap, and we can't use AWS PrivateLink features (endpoint service) across peering. - PrivateLink = AWS-managed ENIs in customer's subnet, no route table edits needed for our service, and customer keeps full control of egress. - For peering, remember to disable
  route propagation on transit gateways if they want explicit control.

Sam Patel: Customer asks if we can supply static egress IPs from our side for their firewall allowlist. Options: 1) Customer routes outbound via their NAT/proxy to internet and allows our hosted endpoints (no static IP requirement on our side), or 2) We run a customer-dedicated egress proxy in their VPC (sidecar EC2/NLB) — requires Dedicated/Private deployment and infra effort, or 3) Use static NAT Gateway with Customer-managed egress through a partner appliance. Which do we want to propose?

Priya Nair: We typically recommend: - PrivateLink + customer NAT/egress proxy (preferred) — simplest security posture. - If they insist on our IPs (allowlist), we can expose a small set of static egress IPs for Dedicated customers with an NLB in the customer's VPC peered to our private infra, but that requires Dedicated capacity and an SLA addendum.

Emily Wong: Pricing check: can we ballpark Dedicated pilot cost for 2x A100-equivalent GPUs for 2 weeks? Customer will want that for demo. Sam/ProdEng — any quick estimate?

Sam Patel: Rough estimate: Dedicated pilot (~2 GPUs reserved) for 2 weeks — ballpark $6k–$10k depending on region and support tier. For Private (on-prem/VPC) licensing and setup + 1-day eng support, add ~$8k–$15k one-time. I'll confirm exact quote offline.

Alex Chen: Security questionnaire asks: "Does Redwood accept inbound connections from customer VPC?" Also question on key management: "Can customer bring their own keys (KMS/HSM)?"

Priya Nair: Answers: - Inbound: Only via PrivateLink endpoints (customer-initiated). No direct public inbound to our control plane for Private deployments. - KMS/HSM: Yes, Private supports customer-managed KMS via IAM + external HSM integrations for on-prem — we'll need SOW and network runbook.

Marco Ruiz: Firewall rules snippet for PrivateLink scenario (customer side):

```
# Allow outgoing to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs
Allow: TCP 443 to ENI IPs for region eu-west-1
# Example ephemeral ports
Allow: TCP 1024-65535 for client ephemeral outbound
# Health probes (if using NLB)
Allow: TCP 443 from our monitoring IPs (we'll provide list)
```

Marco Ruiz: For VPC peering scenario you also need: route table entries to our VPC CIDRs and no overlapping CIDR blocks. We'll provide the exact CIDR list once they sign the NDA/POC agreement.

netops-bot: FYI — internal doc: https://redwood.example.com/internal/presales/networking-guide (read-only) :link:

Alex Chen: Customer also flagged auditing: they want flow logs and audit trails for the POC. Can we enable VPC Flow Logs on the PrivateLink ENIs / customer's VPC?

Priya Nair: Yes — customer can enable VPC Flow Logs and share export to their S3/CloudWatch. For our Private offering we can surface connection logs in the Console (requires higher retention add-on).

Sam Patel: Action items: - @Alex Chen: get customer VPC CIDR(s) + preferred regions + whether they allow PrivateLink. - @Marco Ruiz: prepare approximate CIDR list + sample firewall rules we can hand to the customer's network team. - @Emily Wong: confirm POC budget approval for Dedicated pilot if customer requests static IPs.

Alex Chen: I'll gather details and paste customer's responses here today. Thanks team :thumbsup:
